pathwayLabel: No Direct Path — California's C-36 Is a Contractor License, but Texas Licenses Only Individual Plumbers
examName: TSBPE Journeyman Plumber examination (computer-based + practical) after the standard apprentice route; Master Plumber examination later — the Out-of-State Examination is not available to a C-36 contractor license
steps: Texas TSBPE has no reciprocity agreement with California — its only confirmed signed reciprocal agreement is with Louisiana.

Texas licenses plumbers only as individuals (Tradesman Plumber-Limited, Journeyman, Master, Inspector) — there is no plumbing company or contractor license. California's C-36 Plumbing classification is the opposite kind: a contractor license issued by the Contractors State License Board.

TSBPE's Out-of-State Examination (the shortcut that skips Texas's coursework and job-site-hour requirements) requires a 'current, state-issued Residential, Journeyman or Master plumbing license' held for 2 years. A C-36 contractor license is not a Journeyman or Master Plumber license, so this shortcut does not apply on its face.

The route that remains is Texas's standard one: register as a Plumber's Apprentice ($15), document 8,000 hours of experience under a Texas Responsible Master Plumber (RMP) or a Master Plumber licensed in another state, complete 48 hours of approved classroom training, then pass the Journeyman exam ($40 exam fee, $40 license fee).

Experience gained in California counts toward the 8,000 hours only if it was supervised by a 'Master Plumber licensed in another state' — how TSBPE treats experience under a California C-36 contractor is a case-by-case question its rules do not answer.

To run a plumbing business in Texas, the company must secure at least one Responsible Master Plumber: a Texas Master Plumber (eligible after holding a Journeyman license for 2 years; $175 exam, $75 license) who dedicates the license to that one company ($300 RMP license). A C-36 license does not satisfy this, whatever the company's standing in California.
A failed exam carries a mandatory waiting period before retesting: 30 days after a first failure, 60 days after a second, 90 days after a third or later failure.
notes: Confirmed 2026-09-30 by direct pdftotext extraction of TSBPE's current Out-of-State Examination Application (revised March 2026) and Administrative Rules (March 13, 2026). The Out-of-State Examination requires 'Proof applicant is currently licensed as a Journeyman or Master Plumber in another state' held for two years, and a 'Legible copy of the applicant's current, state-issued Residential, Journeyman or Master plumbing license.' Texas issues only individual licenses (§365.1); a person or company may not offer plumbing to the public unless it 'has secured the services of at least one RMP holding a current Master Plumber License' (§367.9); an RMP is a licensed Master Plumber who lets only one plumbing company use the license (definitions, (47)). Standard route: Journeyman §363.5 (48 classroom hours; 8,000 hours under a RMP or 'a Master Plumber licensed in another state'; plus an Apprentice Registration, Tradesman-Limited license, or out-of-state Journeyman license); Master §363.4 (Journeyman license held 2 years, or 1 year with an approved apprenticeship). Fees per §361.6: Apprentice Registration $15, Journeyman exam $40, Journeyman license $40, Master exam $175, Master license $75, RMP license $300. feeUsd ($95) is the sum of TSBPE's own fees to reach a Journeyman license; Pearson VUE, fingerprinting, and training-provider costs are not included. California side: C-36 is a contractor classification under 16 CCR Division 8, Article 3 (CSLB cites the article, not a section number, on its classification page) (read in full on CSLB's site). needs_review: whether California issues any state-level individual journeyman or master plumber license (which would qualify for the Out-of-State Examination) has not been confirmed from an official source and is not assumed here; and whether TSBPE credits California experience toward the 8,000 hours is not stated in its rules. This record documents the structural mismatch itself — contractor license on one side, individual licenses only on the other — rather than presenting a false equivalence.
officialSourceName: Texas State Board of Plumbing Examiners (TSBPE)
